description:
FILED s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), found probing #565.  PRE-EXISTING and
SILENT.

REPRO:
    $^P = 1;
    { local $^P = 5; print "in=[$^P]\n"; }
    print "out=[$^P]\n";
  perl: in=[5] out=[1]
  PCL:  in=[1] out=[1]      <-- the localized VALUE is lost, silently

Same for $^F, and for $^R now that #565 makes it a real container.  `local $/`
and `local $_` are fine, and so is `local $g` on an ordinary global.

CAUSE (located, one line of emission).  `Pl::Parser::_local_target_item` asks
TWO authorities for a `local` target: `cl` (the storage name) comes from
`_transform_pkg_var`, `place` (the setf place) from the expression lowering.
The header comment there (task #510) says "Measured over every magic name PCL
knows: only $! diverges" -- that measurement missed the caret family.  For
`$^P`:

    cl    = _transform_pkg_var('$^P')  ->  $^P      (BARE)
    place = the lowering               ->  |$^P|    (pipe-quoted)

and the emitted `let` binds the BARE one:

    (let (($^P (p-box-for-local 5)))
      (p-print (p-string-concat "P-local=[" |$^P| "]...")))

Generated code loads under :invert, where an all-upper token reads DOWN-cased,
so `$^P` in the binder is the symbol `$^p` and `|$^P|` in the body is a
DIFFERENT symbol.  The let shadows a name nothing reads; the body keeps reading
the global.  This is exactly the #412 rule ("a caret variable of ANY sigil must
be pipe-quoted") applied everywhere EXCEPT the local storage slot.

`_transform_pkg_var` pipe-quotes on a character class -- ["|;,()\[\]{}'`\\] --
which no caret name contains, so it falls through to `cl_sym`, which is
identity on ASCII.

FIX SHAPE (surgical, one authority):  in `_local_target_item`, when the target
is a Magic token AND the lowering's `place` is a plain SYMBOL (not a call form
like `(p-errno-string)`), use `place` as `cl` too.  That routes both answers
through the ONE authority that already knows the pipe-quote rule, and leaves
`$!` (whose place IS a call form) on its existing special-cased path.  NB it
also rewrites `local $/` from the bare `$/` to `|$/|` -- the SAME CL symbol, so
semantically a no-op, but it WILL show as textual diffs in corpus-diff and the
emission A/B, and every one of those has to be read and explained.  The
narrower alternative is to make `_transform_pkg_var` pipe-quote a name
containing `^`, which is textually inert for every other spelling; it is a
second place that knows the rule, which is why it is the second choice.

BAR: perl-vs-PCL probe of `local` on $^P / $^F / $^R / $^W plus the negatives
($/ , $_ , an ordinary our-global, and `local $!`); a row in
Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t (which currently documents the divergence in its header
and must lose that paragraph in the fixing commit); corpus-diff read in full.
subject: local on a CARET variable is a silent no-op: the let binds the bare symbol $^P while every read emits |$^P| (different symbols under :invert)
